original_card.question: Does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?
methods: Trace one hypothesis through the source, checker and complete caller.
Construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Identify why the timing-only omission passes but the full production controller still rejects it.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one current supplier obligation and trace whether its acceptance depends on an independent check.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Closing a current acceptance gap or proof obligation strengthens reliability even without changing kappa.
allowed_variations: Audit one named current condition using a new semantic counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Reporting the historical timing-only diagnostic as a new current acceptance bug.

actual_scope: Does the local-word frame obligation checked by research/gauge44-frames-x/independent/audit_local.py follow from its source-bound checks for every section of the word? Audited condition: frames of cut gates.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one selected supplier obligation; the audited checker is the local-word auditor used by the selected and the pending T74 supplier lines, and the semantic counterexample is built on the pending T74 supplier base word because that is where the gap appeared.
bottleneck_link: An acceptance gap in the local auditor can admit a word whose paid profile is understated; closing it strengthens every package that relies on this auditor without the native chain. No kappa changes.
stop_rule: Stop after one semantic counterexample, one guard that accepts every genuine word checked and rejects the counterexample, and two mutation controls.
evidence: evidence/AUDIT-BASE.json and AUDIT-PROBE.json (the unchanged auditor passes both); evidence/GUARD-PROBE.json (the four non-centre cut gates); evidence/GUARD-GENUINE-WORDS.json (146 genuine words at the base commit plus the supplier words: no violation); evidence/NATIVE-PROBE.txt (the native chain rejects the probe at hpe_emit_local.py).
author: Marius-Paul Dumitrean
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code): search, construction of the counterexample, code, runs, analysis and text.

open_questions.question: Should the guard become part of a new version of the local auditor (or of the registered replays that call it)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: audit_local.py is pinned by hash in 421 files at the base commit, so it is not changed here; packages that rely on it without the native chain inherit the gap.
open_questions.first_step: Done for the registered packages by ywz65 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2478#issuecomment-6192363481): seven actual callers of the auditor at the base commit; their committed words pass guard.py with the same 176-gate cut. Next: choose how a versioned auditor (or a guard step before it) is adopted by those callers.
open_questions.blocked_by: A maintainer decision on how to version a pinned auditor.

open_questions.question: Do the other unpriced sections (precondition, derived compensation, frame-free cleanup) admit analogous counterexamples?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cut gap shows the auditor trusts structure it does not check; the precondition and cleanup are also frame-free.
open_questions.first_step: For each section, write the structural rule the native emitter assumes and test it against a constructed word as here.
